entities.description: A network or security zone. `access` means an attacker can originate traffic there, not that every member is compromised.
A forwarding and management device. `admin` means administrative control.
The filter managed by one router. Its permissions apply to named flows.
A workstation or server. `user` and `admin` control are distinct.
Client-side software running on a host or router.
A reachable service running on a host or router, with exploit and login routes.
An identity with explicit authentication and grants; no implicit global privileges.
A description of authentication material; `possessed` is the attacker holding it. Never the secret itself.

associations.description: Membership of a network; a machine can be attached to several. Implies no flow permission.
The machine an executable runs on, at `privilege: user | admin`. Each executable has one host.
The firewall a router manages: one each way.
Where a credential is kept: a host at `privilege: user | admin`, an application as `user`. Possession still takes an extraction.
A credential that authenticates an account; any one suffices.
A service that accepts this account for login.
What an account gets on a host (`user | admin`) or router (`admin` only).
Management access to a machine from a network, independent of ordinary forwarding.
A firewall's named permission for a flow: `allowed: true | false | unknown`.

states.description: Traffic can be originated in this network.
This software does what the attacker says.

parameters.description: Time to establish the flow once its source is controlled and its route permitted.
Time to find a usable exploit for a reachable service.
The same, once the service is patched; selected by `defenses.patched`.
Time to turn a found exploit into control of the service.
Time to log in with an account's material, once the service is reachable.
Time to extract the credential from a store the attacker controls.
The same, once the store is protected; selected by `defenses.protected`.
Time to authenticate to a machine's management from an administering network.

rules.output: the named state, attained at time zero
assumptions: A foothold is an attacker input, never an estimate of an initial compromise.
Administrative control of a host includes everything a user can do on it.

rules.prerequisites: the hosting machine at the executable's declared privilege (admin also satisfies user)
assumptions: Controlling a machine at the privilege software runs with is controlling that software.
Router-hosted executables run as admin: this library has no router user state.

rules.output: the hosting machine at the executable's declared privilege
assumptions: Controlling software yields the privilege it runs with and no more: user software never alone grants admin.

rules.prerequisites: host.user or router.admin, for a machine attached to the network
assumptions: Access to a network is the capability to originate traffic in it, not control of its members.

rules.prerequisites: the permission's policy allows the flow, or the managing router is under admin control
rules.output: the flow's permission at that firewall, satisfied
assumptions: A router's admin can bypass its firewall for an explicitly modelled flow.
An unknown policy is an unknown branch, not a denial.

rules.prerequisites: source.control and every permission along the route
assumptions: The route is checked statically; there is no discovery of IP routes, NAT or transitive trust.
Reaching a service is not controlling it.
Patching selects the authored replacement distribution; it does not by itself eliminate every exploit.
Exploit research is not reused across services.
Deployment includes whatever bypass of detection or protection the author assumed in its note; there is no unreported extra success factor.

rules.prerequisites: the storing host at the store's privilege, or the storing application under control
assumptions: Protection selects the authored replacement distribution, not a guarantee.
Possession requires an extraction action even from a controlled store.
Any one authenticating credential suffices; multi-factor authentication is outside this library.
Material alone grants no access.

rules.prerequisites: service.reachable and account.material, for an account the service authorizes
assumptions: Retries and account lockout are outside this library.

rules.prerequisites: account.session at a service, and a grant on the machine that hosts that service
rules.output: the hosting machine at the granted privilege
rules.scope: one per matching session and grant
assumptions: A grant is used only on the machine the service actually runs on; a login on one machine is never control of another.

rules.prerequisites: access to the administering network and account.material, for an account granted on the managed machine
rules.output: the managed machine at the granted privilege
rules.scope: one per administration and grant pair
assumptions: An administration association is explicit permission to attempt management authentication, not a successful login.
An isolated administration zone is not reached just because it administers something.
